## The question

[Beamer: Transparent AND centered background image on intro slide](https://tex.stackexchange.com/questions/108356/beamer-transparent-and-centered-background-image-on-intro-slide), asked by [Dr. Beeblebrox](https://tex.stackexchange.com/users/27498/dr-beeblebrox) on TeX Stack Exchange (2013-04-12; [CC BY-SA 3.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/3.0/)):

> I know this is similar to other questions. Other answers address either:
>
> 1. Adding a transparent image
> 2. Centering an image but I cannot find an answer with both. 
>
> With previous answers I can successfully make my image transparent OR centered, but not both. I've tried integrating methods for the two with no luck.  
>
> Here's the code I'm using on my introduction slide
>
>
>
> ```latex
> \usepackage{tikz}
>
>     \usebackgroundtemplate{ 
>          \vbox to \paperheight
>               {\tikz \node[opacity=0.2] 
>                  {\vfil\hbox to \paperwidth
>                      {\hfil\includegraphics[width=1.5in]{name.png}
>                   \hfil}\vfil} ;  }
>             }
> ```
:::

Combining the work of https://tex.stackexchange.com/questions/74038/transparent-image-background-in-beamer and https://tex.stackexchange.com/questions/3915/image-on-full-slide-in-beamer-package/3927#3927, you can do something like:

```latex
\documentclass{beamer}
\usepackage{tikz}

\usebackgroundtemplate{%
\tikz[overlay,remember picture] \node[opacity=0.3, at=(current page.center)] {
   \includegraphics[height=\paperheight,width=\paperwidth]{example-image-a}};
}

\begin{document}

\begin{frame}
Background transparent image, centered on slide
\end{frame}

\end{document}
```

![sample output][1]

You have to compile twice to get the image centered.
